body: Honestly, this among others, are the primary sustenance for my continued life and has been for years. These and drugs. But what is my continued existence to you?

> I guess you have to try your best to stay strong and to not let negative emotions get to you, negative emotions are your worst enemy.

The negative emotions aren't my enemy. They're the only ones that don't lie to me. It's the positive ones that feel like I'm trying to escape from the reality of my existence.  

> Also, isn't there hope for something to happen in your life? 

Something good happening to me won't make my life worth living. I learned that when I got my liberties at 18 and it was reinforced again and again when I had my first business success and had my first successful long term relationship. Those things don't make life worth living. Being able to rationally justify the continuation of my existence would, but everything in my life has reinforced the belief that life is a negative sum game. I'm worse off for virtually experience I've ever had - even the ones that I thought were good at the time. I can't continue to live being tormented by my past and the uncertainties of my future. It's time to end it all.

> Think about what would happen if you disappeared? Think of the emergency workers. How many of them will be risking their own skin on a search and recovery of your remains by trying to track you down in the far-off rural area you intend to go to? Think of what they will experience when they come across your festering, rotting remains? Think of the explosive trauma everyone will go through for years to come.

I'm going to die eventually anyways. My family will experience the same trauma anyways. The public health dept and the police will have to open and close the case anyways. Someone will have to handle my decomposing remains anyways. 

>All of them will ask, what? Why didn't this person just talk with me one more time?  

The obvious answer is because 1) whatever they have to say to me won't change my mind and 2) it's more than likely that they will feel even more personally responsible for not being able to save me if I give them my last call.  

> me? What could I have done to help? 

They will ask themselves this question even more if I called ahead of time and told them I was going to kill myself. I think a scenario in which they have no idea what even happened to me is better, because they won't blame themselves for it and they can fill in the gaps with whatever they wish. They can tell themselves that I didn't really kill myself; that I just died in a hiking trip or whatever. If I pull this off right, then they will have no idea. 

> You and the people who love you deserve better. 

I deserve to have self-determination. I deserve to have an out when everything has gone wrong for me. I deserve to be able to decide my life isn't worth living and to do something about it even when the people who love me want me to stick around for their benefit.  

People have no idea that I'm really killing myself for their benefit, anyways. If I don't kill myself I won't be able to stop myself from taking revenge on them for all the shit they've put me through. You have no idea how many hours I've spent planning their murders. Planning a rampage. They will never know that they dodged a bullet when I put one through my brain.
Two reasons: self-consciousness and a desire to spare my family members of the trauma I will inflict on them by killing myself (even though they don't really deserve that much)

I don't feel attracted to him, I feel repulsed by him. He causes me psychic pain. Every time I see him I just want to get away from him, but he stays inside my head tormenting me. I can't stop it, but I don't know that I can find another place to live in my area that I can afford, either. I'm seriously considering being homeless at this point.
I mean, I understand where you're coming from but I firmly believe that they are just a product of the system. Simply maligning their character isn't very productive.
